chunks: Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a mosque that is in a house or room, and it appears to its people that they wish to expand it by taking a portion of it, or to move it to another place. He said, 'There is no harm in that.' I said, 'And if a place is used for storage for a time, then it is cleaned and made into a mosque?' He said, 'Throw some dust upon it until it is covered, for that purifies it, if God wills.'

key_terms.الْمَسْجِد: Mosque (specifically a place of prayer, often used for home prayer areas in this context)
key_terms.حَشّاً: Storage or place for storing goods
key_terms.يَتَوَارَى: To be covered or concealed (by the dust)

ai.seo_question: How can a room used for storage be converted into a mosque according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of domestic prayer spaces, permitting both the expansion of existing mosques within a home and the conversion of storage areas into mosques through the simple act of casting dust upon them. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that physical utility does not permanently negate the sanctity of a space, provided proper ritual purification is observed. It highlights the practical ease with which believers can establish dedicated prayer areas in their residences, reflecting the importance of consistent devotion in daily life.
